analysis.title: Nasdaq Futures: Is Length Still Elevated
key_insights: Despite price turbulence over October 13-20, Nasdaq futures Non-Dealer net positioning reached a new nominal high per CFTC Commitment of Traders. Non-Dealers bought $9.5bn while the index lost 3.5%, the 3rd straight week of buying and $21.8bn cumulative since September 29.

On October 22, Meta (-7.0%) led a broad decline in AI-related exposure: HyperScalers -4.1%, Memory -8.6%, Semiconductors -6.5%. Meta forecast significant spending increases, which rattled credit markets already concerned about the sustainability of the debt-fueled AI infrastructure boom.

On October 22 the Nasdaq fell 2.9% and futures aggregate open interest rose $10.6bn, the largest 1-day jump in 2026 excluding roll periods. Funding underperformed, and GS reads this as sizeable shorts being initiated.

From October 22-26 the Nasdaq recouped 1.1% and futures open interest retraced $9bn. Tactical downside shorts were unwound. Funding also cheapened on an outright and relative basis, so longs were cut as well.
CTAs were likely a key driver of the long liquidation, given a momentum break on the GS Futures Strategists' framework.
Length remains elevated heading into more MegaCap tech earnings. If results from Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet fail to impress, meaningful futures selling could follow.
earnings_insights: Meta earnings disappointed (reported around October 22) and the company forecast significant spending increases. Meta fell 7.0% on October 22. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.
Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet results are upcoming (no dates given). The report says that if they fail to impress, meaningful Nasdaq futures selling could ensue.
risk_factors: Elevated Nasdaq futures length leaves the index exposed to selling if Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet earnings disappoint.
Credit market concern about the sustainability of the debt-fueled AI infrastructure boom, aggravated by Meta's higher spending forecast.
Further CTA-driven futures selling if momentum thresholds stay broken.

vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq futures Non-Dealer net positioning hit a new nominal high per CFTC data as of October 20, with $9.5bn bought that week and $21.8bn over 3 straight weeks since September 29.
Futures aggregate open interest jumped $10.6bn on October 22, the largest 1-day increase in 2026 excluding roll periods, then retraced $9bn over October 22-26.
Nasdaq 3-month funding cheapened on an outright basis versus Fed Funds and relative to S&P funding, which GS links to longs being cut.
CTA momentum thresholds on the GS Futures Strategists' framework broke, which GS flags as a likely driver of the long liquidation.

tension_points.bull_case: Non-Dealers kept buying for 3 straight weeks, $21.8bn since September 29, and positioning hit a new nominal high despite price turbulence. The Nasdaq recouped 1.1% October 22-26.
tension_points.bear_case: Length remains elevated after the October 22 selloff, CTA momentum has broken, and Meta's higher spending forecast has rattled credit markets already worried about AI debt. Weak MegaCap earnings could trigger meaningful futures selling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet results failing to impress would invalidate the bull case and could prompt meaningful futures selling.
